items.text: Masoud Pezeshkian spoke about the killing of students in the war. Morteza Kazemian criticized these remarks and referred to the December killings during Pezeshkian's government. He questioned the ethical legitimacy of such statements.

Alireza Beiranvand must be conscripted for military service on the first of Aban. His medical requests, including shoulder injury and referral to the neurology and psychiatry commission, were reviewed but not approved. The location and manner of his service are not yet determined and will be announced in the coming days.

Yesterday, a minibus carrying seasonal workers collided with a car on the Piranshahr to Mirabad route. This accident resulted in injuries to five workers. More details are published by Harana News Agency.

The Houthis launched a deadly attack on Riyadh International Airport. This issue and escalating tensions in the Middle East are the focus of the EU foreign ministers' meeting in Luxembourg. Iran's developments and maritime security are also discussed in the meeting.
A citizen sent a video showing a protest poster next to an ATM in Zanjan. The poster protests the rise in currency prices. He says our money has no value anymore.

Majid Ibn al-Reza, acting Minister of Defense, warned about the dangers of civilizational confrontation and playing with fire. He emphasized that Iran's armed forces are ready to respond and that the US should not play with fire. Ibn al-Reza stated that a civilizational assault cannot force the Iranian nation to retreat.

The judiciary of the Islamic Republic announced the execution of Omar Dorostaran, a member of the Jaish al-Adl group. He was accused of supporting attacks on military bases in Rask and Chabahar counties in Farvardin 1403. The judiciary did not provide any explanation about the trial proceedings.

Messages received by Iran International indicate worsening living conditions for workers and drivers in various cities. Some have not been paid for several months and their insurance has been cut off. The living crisis has intensified alongside rising currency and essential goods prices.

A 33-year-old young man reports severe economic problems and currency devaluation in Iran. He complains about increased theft and insecurity, high inflation, and the social security's failure to pay unemployment insurance. He also points to rising prices of daily goods and declining purchasing power.

Retired telecommunications workers in Khuzestan held a protest march in Ahvaz today. They demanded the implementation of regulation 89/24 and attention to their demands. The protesters objected to the supplementary insurance situation and the arbitrary increase in insurance premiums.

The Israeli Prime Minister discussed the possibility of a military attack on Iran in a meeting with security officials. The Israeli army is preparing for three scenarios: an independent attack, joint operations with the US, and responding to a potential Iranian attack. More details are available in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

The Judiciary Media Center announced the execution of Omar Dorostaran, a security suspect from Rask county. He was identified as a member of an opposition group against the regime. The execution took place today, Monday, October 12.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh spoke about the Islamic Republic's threats against AI centers and US infrastructure in the region. He said these threats may cause costs but do not provide sufficient deterrence to make the US abandon confronting the nuclear program. The US prefers sanctions to take effect in the short term and is not in a hurry for military conflict unless Tehran crosses red lines.

A video shows Arnika Dabag's father visiting her grave on International Day of the Girl. Arnika Dabag, a 15-year-old teenager, was killed on January 9, 2026, in Gorgan. The video was released by Iran International.

Amin Nasser, CEO of Aramco, stated that the global crude oil supply is severely limited and replenishing oil reserves may take up to two years. Aramco is exploring additional export routes and expanding storage capacity. The company also plans to increase gas production capacity by 80% by 2030.

Families of martyrs who lost their daughters during the Iranian national revolution commemorated them on International Day of the Girl. They also spoke about their daughters' bravery in the December protests and continuing their path. This was discussed in an interview with Farnoush Faraji.
A group of retirees gathered in Ahvaz and Kermanshah on Monday, October 12, to protest economic hardships. They chanted slogans against injustice. The protest was held due to living condition issues.

People complain about the difficult economic and social conditions under war, inflation, and rampant price increases. Retired armed forces personnel receive very low pensions, and young people have had to drop out of school to work. The prices of essential goods have risen sharply while their quality has declined.

A Nicaraguan-flagged tanker was attacked by a drone at Sohar anchorage and caught fire. Two of the 11 Indian crew members went missing. India condemned the attacks and is cooperating with Omani authorities to assist the crew.
A 15-year-old Afghan girl and child marriage victim in Mashhad was killed by her 22-year-old husband. The suspect fled after the murder but was later arrested by law enforcement and imprisoned.

The mother of Soda Akramifard said on International Girls' Day that her daughter's wish was for freedom in Iran and the return of Prince Reza Pahlavi. She stated that she will continue her daughter's path. Soda Akramifard, a 16-year-old teenager, was killed on January 9, 2026, in Marlik Malard.

Amnesty International reported that after the killing of protesters in the Woman, Life, Freedom uprising, Iranian authorities harass the families of the victims. This harassment is considered part of crimes against humanity. The Amnesty International report is described as unprecedented.

Masoud Pezeshkian criticized the large bonuses received by managers of state-owned and semi-governmental companies despite heavy losses. He also criticized the interference of various institutions, including the judiciary, in appointments. These remarks were made in an assessment by Arash Azarmi, economic section editor of Iran International.

Philip Luther, the research director of Amnesty International, says the suppression of the families seeking justice in the Women, Life, Freedom uprising has been organized. The Islamic Republic has launched a campaign to intimidate and threaten the families from the beginning.

Following attacks by Houthi forces supported by the Islamic Republic on Saudi Arabia, Al-Nassr team's practice was canceled. Several people were killed and injured in recent attacks on Riyadh airports. Concerns have increased about holding Al-Nassr's match against Neftchi Fergana.

A birthday ceremony for Sarina Saedi, a protester killed in the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising, was held at her grave. Sarina Saedi was a 16-year-old teenager who was killed on October 27, 2022, in Sanandaj.
Students at Bu-Ali University in Hamedan protested on Tuesday, October 12, by placing their food trays on the floor. The protest was against food poisoning incidents and poor food quality.

Mohammad Reza Aref, deputy to Masoud Pezeshkian, emphasized that Iran is an ancient civilization that defends its identity. He warned that the science and technology front is advancing rapidly and enemies will receive a stronger response if they make a mistake. He also criticized the dependence of some Islamic countries' rulers on the West.

Nigel Farage announced that if his party wins the 2029 election, granting asylum to all applicants will be banned for five years. New applications will be automatically rejected and applicants will be returned. He also plans to cancel legal resettlement routes for refugees but exempts Ukrainians.

Milad Mohammadi talks about the killing of his brother Shahriar Mohammadi during the Woman, Life, Freedom uprising. He also discusses the security pressures on their family. This interview reveals details about the situation of the families of the victims.

Reza Zangeneh, a death row prisoner in Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj, has been transferred to solitary confinement. He was sentenced to death by the second branch of the Karaj Revolutionary Court on charges of spying for Israel. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Teachers face severe economic pressure and security monitoring at the start of the new school year. Some teachers say their salaries do not cover basic living and commuting expenses. They have resorted to second and third jobs to meet their expenses.

Rouhollah Najabat stated that the war has entered a new phase where the enemy cannot defeat Iran, nor is a fruitless end to the war imaginable. He warned that some internal statements have given the enemy a chance to regroup. He also said the armed forces' strength has led to a strategic defeat of the enemy and a deadlock for Washington.

Esmaeil Baghayi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, responded to the controversy surrounding his presence at the Arash orchestral event in Spinas Hall, Tehran. He stated that his quick retorts are directed at enemies, not his compatriots. This reaction came after he was booed by the audience.
A video on social media shows a large fire at a boat-building workshop in Piposht, Qeshm. The incident occurred on Monday, October 12. No further details about the event have been released.

Mehdi Alinejad expressed concerns about sending Iran's sports delegation to Saudi Arabia. He mentioned that the war conditions and regional insecurity have delayed decision-making. There are also concerns about hosting the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia.

The mother of Abolfazl Zare joined the campaign "9 apples, 9 months of separation" by placing 9 apples in a dish on the ninth month of her son's death. She said, "I neither forgive nor forget." Abolfazl Zare, 18 years old, was killed on January 9, 2026, in Isfahan.

Following attacks by Iran-backed Houthis on Riyadh airport, several international airlines have canceled or suspended flights to Saudi Arabia. Air France-KLM has extended the suspension of Riyadh flights until November 30. Lufthansa group and other airlines have also canceled or suspended flights until specified dates.

The second week of the trial of three Iranians accused of security actions against Iran International journalists is underway in Woolwich court, London. Prosecutors stated that the Islamic Republic had hired these individuals to monitor and threaten the journalists. More details are provided in an interview with Tajeddin Soroush.

Official sources in Beirut have received warnings about a possible plan attributed to the Islamic Republic to target Joseph Aoun and Nawaf Salam. This news was reported by Mi Farhat, a journalist from Iran International.

Chelsea club and the Spanish Football Federation offer free egg freezing services to female players. This move has been welcomed by FIFPro but concerns exist about pressure on women to delay motherhood. Some athletes have also expressed worries about the motives of sports organizations.

A student showed in a video to Iran International that the cover of their textbook had come off. They described the quality of this year's textbooks as very poor. This issue points to the low quality of the bookbinding.
The interrogation session of Ahmad Rahimi was held at the Mashhad Revolutionary Court. The prosecutor opposed changing his detention to bail. His temporary detention was extended.

Students at Bu-Ali University in Hamedan held a protest on Tuesday, October 12, against food poisoning and poor food quality. They chanted slogans such as "Students die, but do not accept humiliation." This event was captured in videos received by Iran International.

Yahya Rahim Safavi stated that intelligent management of the Strait of Hormuz against the US naval blockade is the main strategy of the Islamic Republic. He described the Strait as an inseparable part of Iran's territorial waters and said restricting passage there is both a right and duty of the armed forces. He also called it a strategic chokepoint in the global energy network.

Belgian tennis player Zizou Bergs defeated Carlos Alcaraz, a seven-time Grand Slam champion, in two sets in the third round of the Shanghai Masters. This defeat secured Alexander Zverev's top ranking in the year-end ATP rankings. Prior to this tournament, Alcaraz had defended his title at the Japan Open.

At least 63 armed incidents were recorded in Sistan and Baluchestan and Kerman provinces from April 1 to October 10, 2026. These events resulted in at least 94 deaths and 33 injuries, with violence escalating to the use of heavier equipment. The main conflict centers are Zahedan, Saravan, Iranshahr, and Rask.

Farhad Bashiri emphasized the need to address the rights of armed forces personnel and retirees in a meeting reviewing the defense minister nominee's plans. He called for clarification of funding sources for these demands and the use of asset monetization to finance the defense ministry. He also stressed the need to revise defense programs and strengthen air defense.

Mojtaba Amani, former ambassador of the Islamic Republic in Beirut, described the incident leading to the deaths of Ebrahim Raisi and Hossein Amir-Abdollahian as suspicious. The incident occurred in Farvardin 1403, coinciding with the escalation of war by Israel. Hassan Nasrallah also considered these events to be divine wisdom.

Prince Reza Pahlavi condemned the Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport that caused dozens of civilian casualties. He expressed condolences to King Salman and the people of Saudi Arabia. Pahlavi stated that the Houthis will end when Iran is free and friendly relations between the two countries are restored.

Hossein Shariatmadari made remarks about the cutting of fiber optic cables in the Persian Gulf. These remarks received widespread and mocking reactions from Iran International's audience. Citizens compared the consequences of this threat to previous positions about closing the Strait of Hormuz.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the country is at a dangerous historical crossroads and current problems cannot be solved solely with military tools. He emphasized the need for a general mobilization and utilizing all capacities to address the issues. Pezeshkian also criticized the gap between claims and actual service to the people.

The UK sanctioned two Iranian citizens, Ruhollah Bazghandi and Shahram Alireza Tamorzadeh Jacki, on charges of espionage and planning attacks. Bazghandi is accused of planning espionage and attacks against individuals outside Iran. Tamorzadeh Jacki is accused of supporting threatening activities abroad.

The government announced that about 40 million people will be eligible for increased credit on the ration card. Reports indicate disruptions in the implementation of this plan. The resources for the ration card plan will be provided from the increase in the official exchange rate.

Mohammad Amin Kholasehshar, 23 years old, was killed on January 8, 2026, in Fardis. His mother said to Pezeshkian that her son was not a terrorist and only wanted to live. She also stated that her other son, Arsalan, ended his life due to grief over losing Mohammad Amin.

Andy Burnham stated that the incident at Fairford Air Base was likely coordinated by Iran and ordered by the IRGC. The UK will impose additional sanctions against the Islamic Republic in response to this incident. Two Iranian citizens were added to the UK's sanctions list for hostile activities.

The birthday ceremony of Pedram Khalooei, a 15-year-old football player, was held at his burial site. Pedram was killed by the suppressive forces of the Islamic Republic during the Iranian National Revolution. He was supposed to participate in the selection tests of Sepahan Academy.

The US military has unveiled a poster identifying the appearance and equipment of Iran's armed forces as a new enemy. This occurred simultaneously with the explosion of two ships in the Persian Gulf and a renewed attack by the Houthis on Riyadh airport. The report was provided by Mojtaba Pourmohsen.

Telecommunications retirees in Isfahan held a protest today as part of the ongoing 'Tuesday protests'. They expressed their objections to the performance of the Imam Khomeini Executive Headquarters and the Cooperative Foundation of the IRGC. The protest took place in front of a telecommunications building in Isfahan.

A group of retirees gathered on Monday, October 12, in the cities of Isfahan and Sanandaj. The protest was held due to livelihood problems. Videos of this gathering have been received by Iran International.

Iranian football representatives in Asian competitions face travel restrictions and loss of hosting rights due to security conditions. Esteghlal reached Doha by government charter flight, and Tractor arrived in Oman after a difficult journey. An interview with Mohammad Taghavi discusses these issues.

The governor of Khuzestan announced that 5,000 students in the province are out of school. This figure reflects the current status of students who have dropped out. The information was published by Harana News Agency.

Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of the parliament, stated that regional countries must confront foreign interventions. He warned that if the territory of these countries is used to attack Iran, a strong response will be given. Nikzad also criticized some countries for cooperating with Iran's enemies.

Human rights activists welcomed the swift removal of the 'Adam and Eve' app by Google and Meta. The app introduced 13-year-old girls as marriage options. Google removed the app on October 9 due to policy violations.

The UK Foreign Office released a joint statement from 29 countries including the US regarding Iran's role in the incident at the Fairford airbase. The statement condemns Iran's violent actions and confirms the IRGC's readiness for hostile activities abroad. It also references recent attacks in Europe and emphasizes legal prosecution.

Ahmad Nadari said that the Gulf countries should stand alongside Iran to maintain regional security. He warned that otherwise, Iran will use its power to force them to accept regional realities. Nadari also emphasized that security cannot be achieved by purchasing weapons and relying on foreign powers.

Felix Sanchez, former coach of the Qatar and Ecuador national teams, has been appointed head coach of the Bahrain national football team. He will start preparing the team for the 2027 Asian Cup from November. Bahrain is in Group B with Jordan, North Korea, and Uzbekistan in the tournament.

The police in Sistan and Baluchestan denied an armed attack on a police station in Rask. However, videos released by an armed group indicate the attack occurred, though this has not been independently confirmed. Mehdi Nakhl Ahmadi states that attacks against government forces continue in Sistan and Baluchestan, and the government is creating security narratives to justify its failures.

The mother of Hamidreza Hosseinipour lit a candle in the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" to commemorate her son. She expressed pride in her son and wished he could see Iran's freedom. Hamidreza Hosseinipour was killed on January 8, 2026, in the Keshan neighborhood of Shiraz.

Ed Miliband, the UK Foreign Secretary, summoned Ali Mousavi, Iran's ambassador in London, following the incident at the Fairford airbase. The UK Prime Minister attributed the incident to the IRGC and announced new sanctions against Iran. Two Iranian citizens were added to the UK's sanctions list for hostile activities.

Ali Mousavi, the Iranian ambassador to the UK, denied any role of Tehran in the incident at the Fairford airbase. He asked the UK government to provide evidence and emphasized readiness for cooperation between the two countries. Mousavi also stated that Iran's condemnation of military attacks against it does not imply involvement in the Fairford incident.

Andy Burnham, the UK Prime Minister, stated in Parliament that the Islamic Republic is responsible for the attack on the Farforod base, which was directed by the IRGC. The US, Australia, Canada, and several other countries issued a joint statement warning that any threats or harm to individuals on their soil by the Islamic Republic are unacceptable. The statement refers to the Islamic Republic's attempts to threaten and intimidate.

A public flogging sentence was carried out for a defendant in a case of assault and committing an indecent act by force in Taybad. This action was taken despite the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights explicitly prohibiting humiliating punishments such as flogging. The execution of this sentence has sparked reactions.

On the early morning of Tuesday, October 12, the execution of a non-political prisoner was carried out in Hamedan prison. The identity of the prisoner was confirmed as Mehdi Mirzaei. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency.

The UK Prime Minister stated that the attack on RAF Fairford was likely coordinated by Iran and directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The UK has threatened to respond using all its powers and impose further sanctions on Iran. Additionally, the Iranian ambassador in London has been summoned to the Foreign Office.

Farzin Nadimi said information about the IRGC plan in the UK is limited. The UK Prime Minister's statements and sanctions on two related individuals indicate a serious threat. This issue may lead to increased security measures in Europe.
A man in Marzdaran town of Tabriz killed his wife and two children. The police commander of Tabriz stated that family problems were the primary cause of this murder.

Foreign ministers of 28 countries, including the US and UK, issued a joint statement condemning Iran's hostile activities abroad. The statement followed the UK Prime Minister's announcement about the IRGC's role in the Fairford base incident. The countries warned that any threats or harm to individuals on their soil will face legal action.

Daily wage workers at the Iran Shahr Burn and Accident Hospital reported that their wages have not been paid for nearly two months. The promised seven-day payment was not fulfilled. Their follow-ups have also gone unanswered.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the university reopening ceremony that the transportation cost of gasoline is 5000 tomans, but it is sold for 1500 tomans. He also mentioned that during the war, powers were given to the governors. Pezeshkian believes that all managers can become president or minister.

The brother of a female political prisoner in Evin Prison was severely beaten and insulted by the meeting hall officials. This incident occurred in the presence of children despite having a visitation permit. Additionally, the visitation time for female political prisoners has been reduced to 20 minutes, and Zahra Karami's phone contact has been cut off for one month.

The British Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, released details of his communications with Manchester City. The information includes official and unofficial meetings and club staff accompanying him on official trips. Burnham expressed concern about the possible sale of the club, and his remarks faced criticism from opposing politicians.

Tractor football team drew 0-0 against Al Shamal in their second match in the Asian Elite League. The match was held in Oman due to the ban on Iranian teams hosting in Asia. Tractor had lost their previous game 1-0 to Shabab Al Ahli.

A prisoner was executed in Khorramabad prison. Two convicts in Tehran and Jiroft were spared execution after the victims' families pardoned them, and the Jiroft prisoner was released after 10 years in prison. Additionally, a murder case in Hamedan was settled through reconciliation.

A memorial birthday ceremony for Alireza Nouri was held at his gravesite with family and close friends present. Alireza Nouri, 29 years old, was killed on the evening of January 9, 2026, in Qazvin. This video was released by Iran International.

Nechirvan Barzani announced that with the start of the war between the US and the Islamic Republic, the Kurdistan Region's border with Iran was closed and forces were deployed. He said that Iranian Kurdish opposition groups were warned not to attack Iran. Additionally, two unidentified drones targeted the Freedom Camp of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups east of Erbil.

Adineh Moradali Beigi, the wife of Mahmoud Beheshti Langaroudi, has been summoned to the third investigative branch of Langaroud Prosecutor's Office. She is accused of propaganda against the regime. Mahmoud Beheshti Langaroudi has also been summoned and charged with a similar accusation.
Azad Rahmati, a citizen from Baneh, was released on Monday, October 12, after posting bail.

Kaja Kallas described the Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport as horrific terrorist acts and said attacks on civilian infrastructure are unjustifiable. She emphasized the importance of escorting ships in the Red Sea and stated that the Aspides naval mission requires at least 10 ships. More than 60 countries have committed to opposing levies on international shipping routes.
